items.title: $SPCX $TSLA $SPY $MU NVDA When a lot of people talk about AI replacing human jobs, what they’re really thinking is, “What will I do if I los
items.content_excerpt: $SPCX $TSLA $SPY $MU NVDA When a lot of people talk about AI replacing human jobs, what they’re really thinking is, “What will I do if I lose my job and can’t put food on the table?” At best, they hope the government will hand out a little “universal basic income,” or UBI, just enough to scrape by. But if you’ve heard Musk repeatedly emphasize the “age of abundance” and “universal high income,” or UHI, over the past two years, you’ll realize that his underlying logic is on an entirely different plane from that of mainstream economists. In Musk’s first-principles thinking, humanity’s future is not about “barely surviving on government handouts.” Instead, we are highly likely to enter an age of superabundance where work becomes purely a personal interest, while material goods are in extreme abundance. Break down this seemingly science-fiction theory, and it really comes down to three extremely dispassionate deductions from physics and economics: 1. The essence of economics is not money, but “output per person.” The reason we usually feel resources are scarce and things are expensive is that human labor is the bottleneck behind every good and service. A doctor can see only a few dozen patients a day, and a worker can tighten only a few hundred screws a day. But once AI takes over all mental labor, and billions of tireless humanoid robots like Optimus take over all physical labor, the production of goods and services on Earth will surge exponentially. 2. The marginal cost of goods and services approaches zero, bringing extreme deflation. Imagine a world where mining, farming, building houses, manufacturing cars, and even performing surgery are all done by solar-powered robots working 24 hours a day, and the cost of human labor has fallen to almost zero. How cheap would goods become? Musk predicts that this will usher in a prolonged period of “super deflation,” with the supply of goods and materials far exceeding the upper limit of humanity’s needs. Everyone will be able to enjoy top-tier healthcare, education, food, and housing at extremely low cost. This is what he calls “universal high income”—not a bigger number in your bank account, but a rise in everyone’s real purchasing power and standard of living to a level that even emperors of the past could not enjoy. 3. How do we get there? Through a hardware loop of “computing power + energy + humanoid robots.” This theory does not rely on politicians printing money and handing out benefits. It relies on the physical infrastructure he is working furiously to build: using AI brains (xAI / Grok) to direct the muscle (Optimus humanoid robots), paired with unlimited energy (solar power and energy storage systems), to produce goods at a frantic pace. He even predicts that humanoid robots will eventually outnumber humans on Earth, with the ratio of robots to humans possibly reaching one-to-one or higher. This army of steel will take on the entire production system that sustains society for all of humanity. Put simply, this is the endgame Musk envisions: in the future, if you want to grow your own vegetables, do woodworking, or write code, you can do it purely as a hobby for experiencing life. But you will no longer be forced to do soul-draining, repetitive work just to pay the rent and put your next meal on the table. Of course, there is still one major human challenge standing in the way of this utopia: once robots have done all the work for us, where will humans who no longer have to struggle to survive find meaning and a sense of accomplishment in life?

items.title: Germany’s Federal Cartel Office has published a merger notification filed by Tesla regarding its proposed acquisition of EMAG, a German manu
items.content_excerpt: Germany’s Federal Cartel Office has published a merger notification filed by Tesla regarding its proposed acquisition of EMAG, a German manufacturer of precision machining systems and gear-cutting equipment used in the actuators of humanoid robots. The proposed acquisition, initially submitted on November 23, could strengthen Tesla’s "Optimus" program by bringing the production of high-precision transmission components—which are critical to the project—in-house. This would grant the company greater control over manufacturing and reduce its reliance on the external supply chain. Another catalyst emerged from a draft agenda for the European Commission, which suggests that EU member states may hold a formal vote to approve Tesla’s driver-assistance system during a meeting scheduled for December 15. This marks the first explicit mention of such a vote on the agenda and represents a significant regulatory step toward the expansion of Tesla’s "Full Self-Driving" (FSD) system in Europe. $TSLA

items.title: Bernstein expects global smartphone shipments to decline 5% in 2027, following a projected 14% contraction in 2026, as soaring memory costs
items.content_excerpt: Bernstein expects global smartphone shipments to decline 5% in 2027, following a projected 14% contraction in 2026, as soaring memory costs continue pressuring demand, particularly for entry- and mid-range Android devices. AI data-center demand has diverted DRAM and NAND production capacity from consumer electronics, pushing memory prices to roughly 3–4 times previous levels. A meaningful industry recovery is unlikely before 2028, when shipments are forecast to rebound 8% as memory-cost inflation eases. Apple is expected to gain market share, with iPhone shipments rising 3% to approximately 250M units in 2027, versus a projected 7% decline for Android. Its 20th-anniversary iPhone redesign and upcoming foldable iPhone Duo could support growth, with the latter expected to ship 10–15M units in its first 12 months, representing around 5% of total iPhone shipments due to manufacturing and component-cost constraints. $AAPL

items.content_excerpt: OpenAI filed counterclaims against Apple in California federal court, accusing the company of stealing trade secrets and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices. OpenAI alleges Apple rehired a former employee who had accessed confidential information about its upcoming AI device and hardware roadmap, potentially to obtain those documents. OpenAI also claims Apple uses employment practices and continued access to former employees’ personal devices and accounts to monitor and intimidate workers joining competitors. The company says approximately 400 former Apple employees have joined OpenAI. Apple denied the allegations, calling the counterclaims an attempt to distract from its own lawsuit filed in July, which accused OpenAI of poaching former employees and misappropriating trade secrets to accelerate its consumer hardware ambitions. Both companies deny the opposing allegations. $AAPL $OPEAZZX.P

Additional support came from Oracle's confirmation that financing for its massive OpenAI data-center infrastructure contract is fully secured following a $20 billion capital raise split equally between equity and senior bonds. A favorable analyst upgrade from Hold to Buy the previous day also supported sentiment, with the analyst arguing that dilution, elevated debt-insurance costs and other headwinds were already more than reflected in the share price. items.title: Palantir Technologies has formally signed a five-year agreement with the Polish Ministry of Defence, valued at approximately $300 million, t
items.content_excerpt: Palantir Technologies has formally signed a five-year agreement with the Polish Ministry of Defence, valued at approximately $300 million, to implement its "Maven Smart System"—an artificial intelligence-based platform designed to assist military commanders with decision-making on the battlefield. The platform, which operates in Poland under the codename "Saturn," is already in use within the command structures of NATO and the United States Department of Defense. Polish Minister of Defence Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz emphasized that all system keys, servers, and data will remain the exclusive property of the Polish Armed Forces, thereby addressing previous concerns regarding data sovereignty. The agreement represents a significant boost to Palantir’s defense strategy in Europe, particularly following the decision by France’s national intelligence agency to terminate its contract with the company in favor of a local provider. $PLTR

items.title: $ENPH Anyone understand if the IQ SST gets tax credits? Here is some comments from AI implying IQ SST would not likely get them. 45X defines
items.content_excerpt: $ENPH Anyone understand if the IQ SST gets tax credits? Here is some comments from AI implying IQ SST would not likely get them. 45X defines an inverter as converting DC "from 1 or more solar modules or certified distributed wind energy systems into alternating current" (§45X(c)(2)(A)). In a data center the IQ SST does the opposite: grid AC to 800 V DC. On a plain reading, no 45X credit. The 11 cents/W microinverter rate (§45X(c)(2)(E)) requires "one solar module", 120-480 V output and max 650 W. A 5.5 kW module on 13.8 kV fails all three. Even as an inverter, a 5 MW unit looks "central" (over 1,000 kW): 0.25 cents/W, about $2,500/MW vs $110,000/MW for micros. Caveat: it's bidirectional, so with solar plus storage it could turn DC to AC. The IRS decides. Badri said on Q2 they're "finalizing those details", so Enphase seems to expect some credit.

items.title: $ENPH $SPWR Why I Believe $SPWR SunPower’s 80% Collapse Is a Massive Market Overreaction After spending considerable time analyzing SunPower
items.content_excerpt: $ENPH $SPWR Why I Believe $SPWR SunPower’s 80% Collapse Is a Massive Market Overreaction After spending considerable time analyzing SunPower, its financials, SEC filings and the sequence of events over the past few weeks, I believe the collapse from $8–9 to around $2 is not only fundamentally unjustified — it is, in my view, bordering on the absurd. Let’s examine what actually happened. All share prices are split-adjusted. November 9 – Resale registration Approximately 33% of the outstanding shares were registered for resale, primarily relating to the $26.2 million September private placement. The market appears to have interpreted this as a massive wave of shares coming up for sale. However, this was a routine registration process that SunPower was contractually obligated to complete under the original September investment agreement. It was not an announcement that investors intended to sell. No new dilution. No deterioration in the underlying business resulting from the registration. No documented evidence of significant selling by the September investors. Market reaction: - November 6: $9.61 - November 9: $8.50 (−11.5%) - November 10: $8.19 (−3.6%) - November 11: $8.03 (−2.0%) - November 12: $7.42 (−7.6%) Total decline: 22.8% before the next major announcement.** In my opinion, the market significantly overreacted to what was essentially a technical and contractual registration process. **November 12 – NT 10-Q filing** After market close, SunPower announced a delay in filing its quarterly report and disclosed a $21.5 million loss figure. Understandably, this triggered significant concerns about the company’s financial performance and credibility. Market reaction: - November 12: $7.42 - November 13: $5.61 (−24.4%) - November 16: $4.31 (−23.2%) - November 17: $3.39 (−21.3%) A staggering 54.3% decline over just three trading sessions following the filing. However, just seven days after the filing, SunPower reported an adjusted operating loss of $4.9 million, explicitly describing it as a correction to the previously disclosed $21.5 million figure. Although the two figures represent different accounting measures and a full reconciliation is still needed, I believe the magnitude of the sell-off was completely disproportionate to the subsequently reported underlying operating performance. **November 16 – Reverse split announcement** SunPower announced a 1-for-35 reverse stock split, effective for trading on November 18. A reverse split does not mechanically destroy shareholder value. It was intended to address Nasdaq’s minimum bid price requirement. While the stock continued to decline on November 16 and 17, these declines may primarily have reflected the ongoing negative reaction to the November 12 filing rather than the reverse split announcement itself. Interestingly, when the reverse split was implemented, the stock actually rallied. Market reaction upon implementation: - November 17: $3.39 - November 18: $4.19 (+23.6%) This suggests that the reverse split itself may not have been the negative catalyst some investors assumed it to be. **November 19 – Preliminary Q3 results** This is where things get particularly interesting. SunPower reported: - Revenue of $65.1 million, up 18.7% sequentially. - Adjusted operating loss of $4.9 million, down from $17.8 million in Q2. - A reduction in headcount from 705 to 640. - An expectation of approximately halving the adjusted operating loss again in Q4. Given the fears created by the November 12 filing, I would have expected the substantially lower adjusted operating loss to trigger a meaningful recovery in the share price. Instead, the stock continued to collapse. Market reaction: - November 18: $4.19 - November 19: $3.80 (−9.3%) - November 20: $2.59 (−31.8%) - November 23: $2.88 (+11.2%) - November 24: $2.57 (−10.8%) - November 25: approximately $2.00 A further decline of approximately 52% from the pre-earnings closing price. **The operational turnaround** Adjusted operating losses: - Q2 2026: $17.8 million - Q3 2026: $4.9 million - Q4 2026: approximately $2.5 million, based on management guidance. If management delivers, this represents an 86% reduction in adjusted operating losses in just two quarters, potentially bringing the company significantly closer to operational break-even in 2027. Meanwhile, the stock has collapsed from $9.61 to around $2 — a decline of approximately 80%. **The valuation** At approximately $2 per share: - Market capitalization: approximately $18.7 million. - Annualized Q3 revenue: approximately $260 million. - Price-to-sales ratio: approximately 0.07x. - Discount to the September private placement price of $8.89: approximately 77.5%. The September investors included T.J. Rodgers, John Doerr’s Foris Ventures and Crosslink Capital. These investors committed substantial capital less than three months ago. **My investment thesis** Consider the sequence of events: A routine, contractually required resale registration was followed by a 22.8% decline, apparently driven by fears of massive selling pressure. A delayed quarterly filing disclosed a $21.5 million loss figure that the company subsequently described as corrected. The stock collapsed another 54.3% over three trading sessions. A mechanically value-neutral reverse stock split was implemented, and the stock actually rallied 23.6%. Preliminary quarterly results showing a significant improvement in adjusted operating performance, together with expectations of further improvement in Q4, were followed by yet another massive sell-off. The cumulative market reaction appears extraordinarily disproportionate to the underlying events. I believe this self-reinforcing chain reaction has resulted in a substantial disconnect between the share price and the underlying operational development of the company. I acknowledge the genuine risks: substantial debt, limited liquidity, accounting uncertainty, potential dilution and disappointing gross margins. However, I do not believe these developments justify an almost 80% reduction in equity value unless the company's financial position is substantially worse than the preliminary results suggest. If the final Q3 results confirm the preliminary figures, liquidity remains sufficient and management delivers on its Q4 guidance, I believe a share price around $8 could be justified even without a major financial restructuring. That would represent approximately 300% upside from current levels. Any successful recapitalization, additional capital injection or meaningful debt conversion could represent an additional catalyst. In my view, the market may be confusing a financially challenged company undergoing an operational turnaround with a company whose underlying business is collapsing. Those are two very different investment cases. I initiated a speculative long position today at $1.95. High risk, but potentially exceptional upside. Time will tell. Personal opinion, not financial advice.

items.title: $ENPH Thanks for this. Let's try to work out some math on the SST. I would start with avoided cost. One sq ft in the data center white s
items.content_excerpt: $ENPH Thanks for this. Let's try to work out some math on the SST. I would start with avoided cost. One sq ft in the data center white space for a standard building and shell costs $400-$700/sq ft. Let's take the more conservative $500/sq ft for calculation sake. On average, a 1GW data center occupies 3.5M to 7M sq ft. For the purpose of this calculation, let's go with a conservative 5M sq ft. 5M sq ft X $500 per sqft = $2.5B So where does all this take us? Unlike all other SiC based systems, the ENPH SST (based on GAN) does not require a battery backup unit (BBU) and/or a UPS (these are high C rate batteries that is required for all SiC based SST's). These occupy up to half the white space of the data center. For calculation sake, let's say they occupy a conservative 40% of the data center space. So the avoided cost attributable to the ENPH SST is as follows: $2.5b X 40% = $1B This is just our starting point. More to come.

But if you’ve heard Musk repeatedly emphasize the “age of abundance” and “universal high income,” or UHI, over the past two years, you’ll realize that his underlying logic is on an entirely different plane from that of mainstream economists. In Musk’s first-principles thinking, humanity’s future is not about “barely surviving on government handouts.” Instead, we are highly likely to enter an age of superabundance where work becomes purely a personal interest, while material goods are in extreme abundance. Break down this seemingly science-fiction theory, and it really comes down to three extremely dispassionate deductions from physics and economics: 1. The essence of economics is not money, but “output per person.” The reason we usually feel resources are scarce and things are expensive is that human labor is the bottleneck behind every good and service. A doctor can see only a few dozen patients a day, and a worker can tighten only a few hundred screws a day. But once AI takes over all mental labor, and billions of tireless humanoid robots like Optimus take over all physical labor, the production of goods and services on Earth will surge exponentially. 2. The marginal cost of goods and services approaches zero, bringing extreme deflation. Imagine a world where mining, farming, building houses, manufacturing cars, and even performing surgery are all done by solar-powered robots working 24 hours a day, and the cost of human labor has fallen to almost zero. How cheap would goods become? Musk predicts that this will usher in a prolonged period of “super deflation,” with the supply of goods and materials far exceeding the upper limit of humanity’s needs. Everyone will be able to enjoy top-tier healthcare, education, food, and housing at extremely low cost. This is what he calls “universal high income”—not a bigger number in your bank account, but a rise in everyone’s real purchasing power and standard of living to a level that even emperors of the past could not enjoy. 3. How do we get there? Through a hardware loop of “computing power + energy + humanoid robots.” This theory does not rely on politicians printing money and handing out benefits. It relies on the physical infrastructure he is working furiously to build: using AI brains (xAI / Grok) to direct the muscle (Optimus humanoid robots), paired with unlimited energy (solar power and energy storage systems), to produce goods at a frantic pace. He even predicts that humanoid robots will eventually outnumber humans on Earth, with the ratio of robots to humans possibly reaching one-to-one or higher. This army of steel will take on the entire production system that sustains society for all of humanity. Put simply, this is the endgame Musk envisions: in the future, if you want to grow your own vegetables, do woodworking, or write code, you can do it purely as a hobby for experiencing life. But you will no longer be forced to do soul-draining, repetitive work just to pay the rent and put your next meal on the table. Of course, there is still one major human challenge standing in the way of this utopia: once robots have done all the work for us, where will humans who no longer have to struggle to survive find meaning and a sense of accomplishment in life?

Palantir Technologies has formally signed a five-year agreement with the Polish Ministry of Defence, valued at approximately $300 million, to implement its "Maven Smart System"—an artificial intelligence-based platform designed to assist military commanders with decision-making on the battlefield. The platform, which operates in Poland under the codename "Saturn," is already in use within the command structures of NATO and the United States Department of Defense. Polish Minister of Defence Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz emphasized that all system keys, servers, and data will remain the exclusive property of the Polish Armed Forces, thereby addressing previous concerns regarding data sovereignty. The agreement represents a significant boost to Palantir’s defense strategy in Europe, particularly following the decision by France’s national intelligence agency to terminate its contract with the company in favor of a local provider. $PLTR

messages.body: $ENPH Anyone understand if the IQ SST gets tax credits? Here is some comments from AI implying IQ SST would not likely get them. 45X defines an inverter as converting DC "from 1 or more solar modules or certified distributed wind energy systems into alternating current" (§45X(c)(2)(A)). In a data center the IQ SST does the opposite: grid AC to 800 V DC. On a plain reading, no 45X credit. The 11 cents/W microinverter rate (§45X(c)(2)(E)) requires "one solar module", 120-480 V output and max 650 W. A 5.5 kW module on 13.8 kV fails all three. Even as an inverter, a 5 MW unit looks "central" (over 1,000 kW): 0.25 cents/W, about $2,500/MW vs $110,000/MW for micros. Caveat: it's bidirectional, so with solar plus storage it could turn DC to AC. The IRS decides. Badri said on Q2 they're "finalizing those details", so Enphase seems to expect some credit.

$ENPH $SPWR Why I Believe $SPWR SunPower’s 80% Collapse Is a Massive Market Overreaction After spending considerable time analyzing SunPower, its financials, SEC filings and the sequence of events over the past few weeks, I believe the collapse from $8–9 to around $2 is not only fundamentally unjustified — it is, in my view, bordering on the absurd. Let’s examine what actually happened. All share prices are split-adjusted. November 9 – Resale registration Approximately 33% of the outstanding shares were registered for resale, primarily relating to the $26.2 million September private placement. The market appears to have interpreted this as a massive wave of shares coming up for sale. However, this was a routine registration process that SunPower was contractually obligated to complete under the original September investment agreement. It was not an announcement that investors intended to sell. No new dilution. No deterioration in the underlying business resulting from the registration. No documented evidence of significant selling by the September investors. Market reaction: - November 6: $9.61 - November 9: $8.50 (−11.5%) - November 10: $8.19 (−3.6%) - November 11: $8.03 (−2.0%) - November 12: $7.42 (−7.6%) Total decline: 22.8% before the next major announcement.** In my opinion, the market significantly overreacted to what was essentially a technical and contractual registration process. **November 12 – NT 10-Q filing** After market close, SunPower announced a delay in filing its quarterly report and disclosed a $21.5 million loss figure. Understandably, this triggered significant concerns about the company’s financial performance and credibility. Market reaction: - November 12: $7.42 - November 13: $5.61 (−24.4%) - November 16: $4.31 (−23.2%) - November 17: $3.39 (−21.3%) A staggering 54.3% decline over just three trading sessions following the filing. However, just seven days after the filing, SunPower reported an adjusted operating loss of $4.9 million, explicitly describing it as a correction to the previously disclosed $21.5 million figure. Although the two figures represent different accounting measures and a full reconciliation is still needed, I believe the magnitude of the sell-off was completely disproportionate to the subsequently reported underlying operating performance. **November 16 – Reverse split announcement** SunPower announced a 1-for-35 reverse stock split, effective for trading on November 18. A reverse split does not mechanically destroy shareholder value. It was intended to address Nasdaq’s minimum bid price requirement. While the stock continued to decline on November 16 and 17, these declines may primarily have reflected the ongoing negative reaction to the November 12 filing rather than the reverse split announcement itself. Interestingly, when the reverse split was implemented, the stock actually rallied. Market reaction upon implementation: - November 17: $3.39 - November 18: $4.19 (+23.6%) This suggests that the reverse split itself may not have been the negative catalyst some investors assumed it to be. **November 19 – Preliminary Q3 results** This is where things get particularly interesting. SunPower reported: - Revenue of $65.1 million, up 18.7% sequentially. - Adjusted operating loss of $4.9 million, down from $17.8 million in Q2. - A reduction in headcount from 705 to 640. - An expectation of approximately halving the adjusted operating loss again in Q4. Given the fears created by the November 12 filing, I would have expected the substantially lower adjusted operating loss to trigger a meaningful recovery in the share price. Instead, the stock continued to collapse. Market reaction: - November 18: $4.19 - November 19: $3.80 (−9.3%) - November 20: $2.59 (−31.8%) - November 23: $2.88 (+11.2%) - November 24: $2.57 (−10.8%) - November 25: approximately $2.00 A further decline of approximately 52% from the pre-earnings closing price. **The operational turnaround** Adjusted operating losses: - Q2 2026: $17.8 million - Q3 2026: $4.9 million - Q4 2026: approximately $2.5 million, based on management guidance. If management delivers, this represents an 86% reduction in adjusted operating losses in just two quarters, potentially bringing the company significantly closer to operational break-even in 2027. Meanwhile, the stock has collapsed from $9.61 to around $2 — a decline of approximately 80%. **The valuation** At approximately $2 per share: - Market capitalization: approximately $18.7 million. - Annualized Q3 revenue: approximately $260 million. - Price-to-sales ratio: approximately 0.07x. - Discount to the September private placement price of $8.89: approximately 77.5%. The September investors included T.J. Rodgers, John Doerr’s Foris Ventures and Crosslink Capital. These investors committed substantial capital less than three months ago. **My investment thesis** Consider the sequence of events: A routine, contractually required resale registration was followed by a 22.8% decline, apparently driven by fears of massive selling pressure. A delayed quarterly filing disclosed a $21.5 million loss figure that the company subsequently described as corrected. The stock collapsed another 54.3% over three trading sessions. A mechanically value-neutral reverse stock split was implemented, and the stock actually rallied 23.6%. Preliminary quarterly results showing a significant improvement in adjusted operating performance, together with expectations of further improvement in Q4, were followed by yet another massive sell-off. The cumulative market reaction appears extraordinarily disproportionate to the underlying events. I believe this self-reinforcing chain reaction has resulted in a substantial disconnect between the share price and the underlying operational development of the company. I acknowledge the genuine risks: substantial debt, limited liquidity, accounting uncertainty, potential dilution and disappointing gross margins. However, I do not believe these developments justify an almost 80% reduction in equity value unless the company's financial position is substantially worse than the preliminary results suggest. If the final Q3 results confirm the preliminary figures, liquidity remains sufficient and management delivers on its Q4 guidance, I believe a share price around $8 could be justified even without a major financial restructuring. That would represent approximately 300% upside from current levels. Any successful recapitalization, additional capital injection or meaningful debt conversion could represent an additional catalyst. In my view, the market may be confusing a financially challenged company undergoing an operational turnaround with a company whose underlying business is collapsing. Those are two very different investment cases. I initiated a speculative long position today at $1.95. High risk, but potentially exceptional upside. Time will tell. Personal opinion, not financial advice.

$ENPH Thanks for this. Let's try to work out some math on the SST. I would start with avoided cost. One sq ft in the data center white space for a standard building and shell costs $400-$700/sq ft. Let's take the more conservative $500/sq ft for calculation sake. On average, a 1GW data center occupies 3.5M to 7M sq ft. For the purpose of this calculation, let's go with a conservative 5M sq ft. 5M sq ft X $500 per sqft = $2.5B So where does all this take us? Unlike all other SiC based systems, the ENPH SST (based on GAN) does not require a battery backup unit (BBU) and/or a UPS (these are high C rate batteries that is required for all SiC based SST's). These occupy up to half the white space of the data center. For calculation sake, let's say they occupy a conservative 40% of the data center space. So the avoided cost attributable to the ENPH SST is as follows: $2.5b X 40% = $1B This is just our starting point. More to come.
